chunks: Muhammad ibn Uthman ad-Duhni narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far ar-Riqqi narrated to us, saying: Eesa ibn Yunus narrated to us, from Mujalid ibn Sa'eed, from ash-Sha'bi, from Masrooq, who said:

We were with Ibn Mas'ood when a man asked him: 'Did your Prophet tell you how many caliphs would be after him?' He said: 'Yes. And no one has asked me this before you, and you are the youngest of the people in age. I heard him saying: After me, there will be as many as the number of the chieftains of Moses.'
ai.seo_question: How many caliphs will succeed Prophet Muhammad according to the hadith of Ibn Mas'ood?
ai.summary: This narration from Ibn Mas'ood, cited in Al-Nu'mani's *Kitab al-Ghayba*, links the post-Prophetic leadership to the twelve chieftains of Bani Israel mentioned in the Quran, a key hadith used by both Sunni and Shia scholars to substantiate the number of Imams. The term 'nuqaba' (chieftains/plural of naqib) specifically evokes the twelve tribal leaders appointed by Moses, reinforcing the Shia doctrine of twelve divinely appointed successors. This connection serves as a theological bridge between the Mosaic tradition and the Islamic Imamate, emphasizing continuity in divine guidance.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (1) Muhammad bin Uthman ad-Duhni narrated from Abdullah bin Ja’far ar-Riqqi from Eessa bin Younus from Mujalid bin Sa’eed from ash-Shi’bi that Massrooq had said:

Once we were with Ibn Mass’ood in his house when someone asked him: “Had your prophet told you how many caliphs would be after him?” Ibn Mass’ood said: “Yes, he had. But no one has asked me such a question before you. You are the youngest of these people. I have heard the Prophet (S) saying: “After me there will be (caliphs) as the number of the chieftains of Prophet Moses (as).”
